recommendation: Keep the no-change audit. Do not broaden this issue into Resource.id changes or historical release-cache edits; if old R4/R5 publication artifacts need technical correction, handle that through the publication/generator path and the already-audited related issues.
issue_request: FHIR-22493 was a Published/Persuasive FHIR-I change request raised against STU3/R4 type profiles and applied for R5. It asked that type profiles derived from Element repeat the base Element.id special primitive/system type metadata in snapshots instead of replacing it with a plain FHIR datatype such as string.
initial_application: No current FHIR source commit directly referencing FHIR-22493 was found. The R4 history cache still illustrates the original mismatch between Element.id's special json/xml/rdf type extensions and string.id's plain string code. Later generation shifted this family to FHIRPath System.String plus structuredefinition-fhir-type, with follow-up tooling issues FHIR-36036, FHIR-38684, and FHIR-41183 covering remaining id-vs-string propagation defects.
additional_context: The active source/fhir.ini keeps Element, BackboneElement, and ElementDefinition in current build scope. source/datatypes/element.xml declares Element.@id as type string, BackboneElement derives from Element without a separate @id row, and source/elementdefinition.html documents the FHIRPath System.String plus structuredefinition-fhir-type representation. Related final decisions keep Resource.id distinct: Resource.id remains fhir-type id, while Element-derived ids remain fhir-type string.
reconciliation: No FHIR source change was made. Current build.fhir.org profile JSON for Element.id, string.id, Address.id, BackboneElement.id, and ElementDefinition.id all emits code http://hl7.org/fhirpath/System.String with structuredefinition-fhir-type valueUrl string, so the seed requirement is satisfied in the current specification.

related_jiras.note: Published correction establishing that Resource.id should use structuredefinition-fhir-type id, preventing an overbroad Element.id-style string change to resource logical ids.
Published clarification documenting the FHIRPath System.String plus structuredefinition-fhir-type representation used by special elements.
Published tooling issue for Element/BackboneElement-derived id metadata; already represented on the combined branch and confirms current output is corrected.
Published follow-up for Element.id still showing fhir-type id; already represented on the combined branch and confirms current Element.id output is string.
Applied follow-up for ElementDefinition.id in R5; already represented on the combined branch and records that the fix is present in R6/current output.
Later no-change decision explaining why Element.id remains fhir-type string while Resource.id remains fhir-type id.
